description: The Universal Licensing System is the FCC's system for applications and licences in the wireless radio services, and its public data downloads give every licence and application in pipe-delimited files. Licence data cover services such as cellular, personal communications, advanced wireless services, the 700 MHz and 600 MHz bands, microwave point-to-point links, land mobile radio, paging, amateur and maritime, with licensee, call sign, frequencies, locations of transmitters and antennas, market areas and status dates; weekly complete files per service (for example the microwave file of about 211 MB) and daily transaction files are published. Coverage: the United States and territories, current and historical licences. Format and access: ZIP archives of pipe-delimited text on data.fcc.gov/download/pub/uls, plus online search and maps, free as US government data; the portal also lists ULS 3650 MHz base station locations. Caveats: the relational layout needs the FCC data dictionaries; licences show authorisation, not built sites; www.fcc.gov pages refuse scripted access. Simulation uses: spectrum holdings and microwave backhaul links as network topology for telecom, utility and public safety networks, and licensed site locations for hazard exposure. Related records: the FCC antenna structure registration gives towers, and ANFR and ISED give other national registers.
